FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Abrasive Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production Engineering Division Council. This standard is being issued with a view to establish a uniform system of marking of diamond/ cubic boron nitride abrasive products to designate their various characteristics. Marking on smaller wheels ( < 76-2 mm ) has been taken up based on the present practices followed in the country. The usefulness of a uniform system of designation and marking for bonded abrasive products has been recognised by manufacturers and users. The main difficulty, as far as this standard is concerned, lay in the fact that similarly marked grinding wheels produced by different manufacturers do not necessarily give the same results while in use. It is, therefore, emphasized that this standard applied solely to the marking systems and not to Grinding wheels with the same standard the performance of the grinding wheel in operation. symbols but from different source may, therefore, behave differently from each other when in use. As a result of adoption of this standard, it is hoped that markings on wheels of different makers include, if possible, the following information in their would be similar. Users may, therefore, enquiry or order or both to facilitate supply of replacements: a) Name of the manufacturer of grinding wheel of segment previously b) Markings on the wheel or tags supplied witb it. used; and

While preparing this standard, assistance has been taken from the details provided by the manufacturers of abrasive products and ANSI B74. 13-1982 `Markings for identifying grinding wheels and other bonded abrasives' issued by American National Standards Institute (USA).

B - Cubic Boron Nitride D - Diamond 4.1.1 Where it is necessary to designate some particular variation of any one of these types, the manufacturer may use in addition a special symbol (sequence 0 at Fig. 1) preceding symbol 1 ( see also 3.1 ). 4.2 The grain size is designated by a number for which reference shall be made to IS 10960 ( Part 1 ) : 1984. 4.2.1 Wherever required, the manufacturer may follow the grain size number with a symbol indicating combination of different grain sizes. 4.3 Grades The grade is indicated by a letter of the alphabet from A to Z, A being the softest and Z the hardest grade. 4.4 Concentration The use of concentration symbol is optional. The concentration symbol is the manufacturer's designation which defines relative grain spacing. The preferred concentrations are 50, 75, 100, 120 and 150. 4.5 Bond The type of bond following letters: BMv1 Resinoid Metal Vitrified shall be designated by the

Most diamond and CBN wheels are made with a depth of impregnation of diamond/CBN grains. Each grinding wheel manufacturer is at liberty to use the symbol at sequence 8 in

5.2 When grinding wheels are too small ( < 76.2 mm ) in diameter to permit the use of the complete marking, abrasive ( grain ) size and grade symbols alone may be used on the wheel, or the marking on the wheels may be omitted entirely. In the latter case, the complete marking shall be indicated on tags or labels accompanying the wheels in each container 5.3 Keeping in view the importance of the safety requirements, the labels marked with the maximum operating speed in RPM, shall be fixed on the grinding wheel. Where loose labels or tags are accompanying the grinding wheels, the maximum operating speed shall be stencilled on the grinding wheel. However wheels with outside diameter less than 76.2 mm need not be marked with the maximum operating speed.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau ofl&zn Standards Act, 2986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys she assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by Details of conditions under BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
